result.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
result.summary: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, existing approaches typically decouple two inherently related decisions: where to intervene and how to modify the selected components. Such sequential optimization may be suboptimal because the optimal intervention location can depend on the intervention applied there, and vice versa. In this work, we introduce AttentionSwitch, the first jailbreak defense to jointly optimize intervention sites and strengths within a frozen LLM. Specifically, AttentionSwitch learns a sparse set of attention heads together with query-conditioned multiplicative scaling factors, allowing the outputs of the selected heads to be either attenuated or amplified without altering the directions of their representations. Across popular language models and jailbreak attacks, AttentionSwitch outperforms existing defenses, with particularly strong results when training data is scarce.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 AttentionSwitch，在冻结 LLM 上联合学习一组稀疏注意力头及其 query 条件化的乘性缩放因子，对选中头的输出做衰减或放大而不改变表示方向，用于越狱防御，并在数据稀缺时表现较好。
AI.relevance_reason: 其联合进行稀疏头定位与强度缩放的做法，可能为 LVR 中定位承载视觉证据的头部并做定向调制或贡献分配提供方法线索，但论文面向安全防御、无多模态推理实验，需核查其选择机制能否迁移。
